title: bn254-gt-dlp: rho-tower with a constant-time step and a 31,302-instruction static step price, 2^130.091157

claims.statement: For the full-production bn254-gt-dlp target, the single-trial 32-adding Pollard-rho algorithm of proof.md returns x with g^x=z with success probability at least 0.85 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, and every run performs at most W < 2^130.091157 units (log2 W = 130.091156869), where one unit is C=20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents. The walk step is constant-time: its compiled call graph contains no conditional branch, no loop and no early return, so one step costs exactly 31,302 instructions on every input, a static count from the shipped disassembly (STATIC_BOUND.txt; Callgrind confirms 31,302 Ir on every step of 10 production tables). Scalars are drawn by a capped SHA-256 counter-mode rejection sampler (at most K=64 attempts per scalar, abort counted as failure, union bound 66*(1-r/2^256)^64 <= 2^-13.30). Uniformity, independence, the 1/r degeneracy argument and the delta^K abort bound are exact in the ideal independent-word model and heuristic with additive distinguishing advantage eps under the standard PRF assumption for the SHA-256 counter-mode stream; the sampler accepts strictly v<r, so v=r is rejected. The success probability is a random-map heuristic supported by small-subgroup evidence at order 43,913, not a production measurement. This is a reproducible baseline; we assert no comparison to any other submission or frontier.

experiments.purpose: Recompute every ledger row from the profile order r and the static per-step price (31,297 instructions); check the declared rational is the rounded-up log2(W); recompute and check the capped sampler failure bound, measure the sampler's acceptance rate and attempt counts; verify the Python mixer transliteration reproduces the shipped binary's hashdump indices; and run the 32-adding walk (shipped encoding, mixer and tower) in the order-43,913 subgroup of the real BN254 Fp12, reporting successes, no-collision and wrong-recovery counts and the Wilson interval. The constant-time step and its instruction count are checked separately by static_count.py and crosscheck.c.
